mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 9.5%, it signals a weak labor market that may prompt central bank intervention, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate policy support.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 220), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220, or Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a weakening in the real economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 500, it signals a contraction in the housing sector that reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 500, or Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days as investors price in recession risks.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 9.5%), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
